From the conversation history, it seems like there was confusion about which president this was referring to and whether that president had any children.

First, I remember that the Versailles Treaty was signed after World War I, and it was rejected by the U.S. Senate. The president at that time was Woodrow Wilson. So, the president in question is Woodrow Wilson.

Now, the next part is figuring out if Woodrow Wilson had any children. From what I recall, Woodrow Wilson was married to Edith Bolling Galt Wilson, but they didn't have any biological children together. There were rumors that he had an adopted son, but I think those have been debunked over time. Historical records and credible sources indicate that Woodrow Wilson didn't have any children, either biological or legally adopted.

Looking back at the conversation, the Planner initially thought it was Warren G. Harding, which was a mistake. Then, after correcting that, the focus was on Woodrow Wilson and confirming whether he had any children. The WebSurfer agent was doing the research, but there was a lot of back-and-forth as they were trying to confirm the details.

I think the mistake here was that the Planner first incorrectly identified the president as Warren G. Harding instead of Woodrow Wilson. This mistake led to a lot of confusion and unnecessary research about Harding's children, which wasn't relevant to the original question. The Planner should have cross-verified the information more thoroughly before making that assumption.
